$comment: The ffmpeg Offstream ships. Pinned rather than tracked: 'latest' is a moving target,
and an encoder that changes between two builds of the same Offstream version turns a
reproducible bug into an unreproducible one. Nothing here is fetched at build time
LGPL, not GPL. This build is configured without --enable-gpl and with --enable-version3,
which makes it LGPL-3.0-or-later. Every encoder Offstream needs is present: libmp3lame,
libopus, and native flac and aac. A GPL build would drag Offstream's own licensing along
with it, and buys nothing this app uses.
The whole zip is 146 MB and holds ffmpeg, ffprobe, ffplay and the HTML manual. Only
ffmpeg.exe and the licence are bundled - ffprobe is used by the integration tests and
nothing in the app, and shipping it would add another 108 MB to every download.
sourceCommit is the obligation, not a courtesy: distributing LGPL binaries means
distributing the source they were built from. The release attaches that archive rather
than promising it on request, so the offer cannot outlive whatever was going to host it.
